tags: why do dogs beg for food
script: Dinner time arrives and there's your dog, sitting perfectly, eyes locked on your fork. Begging is one of those habits that owners often blame on greed, but it's actually a brilliantly simple learning loop. Dogs are scavenging animals by nature, so food that comes from humans is a great opportunity. If your dog ever got a bite after begging, even once, the behavior is rewarded, and the most powerful kind of reward is the unpredictable one, since dogs keep trying because it might work this time. Your food also smells far more exciting than kibble, and they're picking up on aromas you can't even detect. Boredom and attention seeking play a role too, because sitting next to the table is an easy way to get involved with the family. The fix is consistency. Give your dog something better to do, like a mat or a chew toy during meals, reward calm behavior away from the table, and make sure everyone in the house follows the same rule. Slipping scraps just once resets all the progress. With patience, begging fades, and dinner becomes peaceful again.
